claims.what: Miller's planet time dilation: hours on the planet to years on Earth
claims.note: Line paraphrased: every hour on that planet is seven years back on Earth. A second line 'Seven years per hour here' is also in the transcript, speaker unlabeled. s3 also states the ratio but attributes no speaker. s1 only says time is severely dilated, no ratio (source difference, not a conflict).

claims.what: Time elapsed on Earth/Endurance while the landing party was on Miller's planet
claims.note: Transcript labels TARS as giving it after an unlabeled 'how many years' question; Romilly's preceding line is 'By now it must be...'. The guess that Romilly says it is NOT supported by this transcript. s1 and s3 give '23 years' only.

claims.what: Years elapsed on Endurance while landing party was away
claims.note: s1: 23 years have elapsed on the Endurance. s3 says the same.

claims.what: 23y 4m 8d expressed in days (derived by Proteus, not stated anywhere)
Hours the landing party spent on Miller's planet
claims.note: Derived only: 23.35 years / 7 years per hour is about 3.3 hours. No hour count for the surface visit is spoken in the transcript (s2). CONFLICT: s3 says the party spent 'about one hour' on the planet (and calls the 3 hour figure inferred); the arithmetic with the stated 23y and 7y/hour does not support one hour. Treat 3.3 h as derived, not canon.

claims.who: unlabeled in transcript, likely Cooper or Brand
claims.note: Paraphrase: this manoeuvre will cost us 51 years. s1 and s3 state 51 years too. s1 attributes it to time dilation. Reply line in transcript: 'pushing 120' (unlabeled).
Paraphrase: 'Actually, you are 124 years old.' s1 and s3 do not mention 124.
s1 cast list: 10-year-old Murph. s3 says she is 10. In s2 the line 'My daughter was 10 years old' is attributed to Brand by context, so a spoken mention may exist but attribution is uncertain.
No number spoken in s2; she is only 'far too old'. s1 says elderly Murph. s3: not stated. Inference only.

claims.what: Murph's video message: she is now the age Cooper was when he left
claims.note: Paraphrase: today I am the age you were when you left. No number given. She also recalls Cooper saying they might be the same age. Cooper's own age at departure is not stated in s1-s3.

claims.what: Tom's age when messages are played
claims.note: No numeric age or year count found in Tom's messages (s2); s3 only says teenage son. Do not assert an age.

Paraphrase: we calculated two years to Saturn. s1: crew goes through wormhole after a two-year voyage. CONFLICT inside s2: TARS also says fourteen months to Saturn (and eight months to Mars). Not verified which is the later or current estimate.

claims.what: How long ago the wormhole appeared
claims.note: s1 also says 48 years earlier a wormhole appeared near Saturn. s2 also has 'almost 50 years ago' for gravitational anomalies.

claims.what: When the first people were sent through the wormhole
claims.note: Paraphrase: we sent people into it ten years ago.

claims.what: Life support in each Lazarus landing pod
claims.note: Paraphrase: each pod had two years of life support.

claims.what: Mann's planet day and night length
claims.note: Days are 67 hours long and nights 67 colder hours. No duration given for the crew's stay or for Mann's cryosleep in s1 or s3.

claims.what: Hours TARS asked about before leaving Miller's planet
claims.note: Line is 'TARS, 72 hours, yeah?' with unclear context in the fetch; low confidence.
